articles.title: Mikel Merino: "Vi sangre, humo, gritos... Tengo suerte de estar vivo"
articles.standfirst: Mikel Merino recuerda el ataque con bombas que sufrió en el autobús del Borussia Dortmund en 2017 en el que resultó herido Marc Bartra
articles.summary: Mikel Merino recuerda el ataque con bombas que sufrió en el autobús del Borussia Dortmund en 2017 en el que resultó herido Marc Bartra
articles.body: Mikel Merino, centrocampista del Arsenal que tuvo un papel crucial para que España ganase el Mundial 2026 con España, ha confesado que se siente "afortunado de estar vivo" después de que su "ángel de la guarda" evitara que resultara herido en el atentado contra el autobús del Borussia Dortmund en 2017. En el ataque perpetrado por Sergej Wenergold, en el que detonó tres artefactos explosivos que escondió cerca de unos setos al paso del autobús del equipo alemán mientras este se dirigía a un partido de la Champions League contra el Mónaco, resultaron heridos el defensa español Marc Bartra (tuvo que ser hospitalizado por una lesión en la mano) y un policía que no pudo volver a trabajar. "Creo que tengo un ángel de la guarda. De hecho, tengo suerte de estar vivo", confesó Merino, que en el momento del atentado tenía 20 años, en una carta publica en 'The Players' Tribune' que ha titulado "A las personas que me llevaron en brazos". Mikel Merino recuerda que "seguramente mucha gente joven ni se cree que pasara, o lo grave que fue, pero nos marcó a todos. Hubo un ruido ensordecedor y luego recuerdo que el autobús casi vuelca. Miré hacia atrás y vi sangre en el suelo. Humo, gritos. Recuerdo estar en el hospital esa misma noche, esperando a Marc Bartra, que tenía la muñeca destrozada". "Al día siguiente, alguien me contó que un trozo enorme de metralla había quedado incrustado en el reposacabezas del asiento situado junto al de Marc Bartra. Mi sitio de siempre. Ese día, ese asiento estaba vacío... Sentía las piernas un poco agarrotadas y, como los asientos de la parte delantera se podían reclinar, me senté allí; puede que eso me salvara la vida. Así que sí, creo firmemente que las cosas suceden por una razón", desveló. Las bombas de fabricación casera contenían clavos metálicos y tenían un radio de alcance de unos 100 metros. Sergej Wenergold, el autor del ataque, fue acusado de 28 cargos de intento de asesinato y condenado a 14 años de prisión. En el juicio confesó que no tenía intención de matar a nadie, y que ejecutó el ataque para ganar dinero apostando a una caída en la cotización bursátil del Borussia Dortmund. Marc Bartra habló en 2017 en el programa 'El Hormiguero' de Antena 3 sobre el atentado que sufrió el autobús del Borussia Dortmund. "Cuando iba en la ambulancia, me daba igual que me cortaran el brazo, sólo pensaba en que estaba vivo. Tenía muchísimo dolor en el brazo. Cuando el médico me dijo tras la operación que en un mes podría jugar, fue algo increíble. Tuve suerte de que fuera una fractura limpia que no afectó a los tendones y ni a los ligamentos. Es increíble lo que pueden llegar a hacer los médicos", el contó el actual futbolista del Real Betis a Pablo Motos. "Son las 19 de la tarde, bajamos desde el hotel al autobús. Subimos, fui de los últimos, súper tranquilo, iba a hacer lo que más me gusta. La gente estaba concentrada, era un partido importante. Siempre me siento en el mismo sitio, en la parte de atrás, a la derecha. Yo estaba con el móvil y en un abrir y cerrar de ojos paso de la tranquilidad y el silencio a abrir los ojos y a ver mucho humo. Los oídos me pitaban, no oía nada. Hay mucho olor a pólvora y siento un viento muy caliente en la cara. El móvil se disparó, recibí como un balazo, que es la metralla. En ese momento vi las caras de mis compañeros, me entró mucho miedo, no sabíamos qué pasaba. Intuía que la gente decía que fuéramos al suelo. No podía ni moverme, me quedé paralizado. Fueron todas de golpe, no sé, estaba en el suelo con mucho dolor de cabeza, muy mareado, la mano como que me colgaba, no podía moverla. Grité de dolor y de miedo, no sabíamos si movernos o no, si vendrían más. Vino la fisio y yo me quería dormir, no me sentía bien del dolor, de lo mal que estaba. La fisio me dio unos guantazos, "no te duermas Marc", me decía y me di cuenta de que no me podía dormir, que si te duermes igual no te despiertas. Empecé a pensar en mi hija, estate tranquilo, con los ojos abiertos, te necesitan. Vino la ambulancia y fueron 15 minutos o 10 que pasaron eternos". "La fisio me decía "estate fuerte, no te duermas", pero me lo decía llorando y mirando la ventana, ese era el problema. Por suerte no vino nada más. La gente no es consciente de lo que vivimos en Alemania y en España aún menos. No se lo deseo a nadie. Lo siguiente era no estar ahí. Yo mi pensamiento era primero si estaba vivo o no. Si me podía mover o no. Estaba en shock, los oídos pitando, mareándome. Luego ya vi que podía mover las piernas, pero me dolía muchísimo el brazo. Me sangraba muchísimo. Los fisios no quería bajar del bus. Tardaron más, me pusieron un torniquete con la chaqueta. Me acuerdo de todo y me siento fuerte contándolo". Mike Merino recordó ese terrorifico momento reflexionando en 'The Players' Tribune' sobre lo mal que lo pasó cuando "una fractura de estrés en el pie derecho" casi le deja sin Mundial. "El pasado febrero me tocó ver el PowerPoint más deprimente de mi vida. Estaba en un despacho de la ciudad deportiva, con una bota ortopédica. El doctor del club y el jefe de fisios iban pasando diapositiva a diapositiva. "Como se ve en esta imagen, es una fractura de estrés en el pie derecho…"... Estábamos peleando la Premier. El Mundial estaba a la vuelta de la esquina. Mi mujer estaba embarazada. Yo pensaba: Vale, lo pillo. ¿Cuánto tiempo? El doctor me dijo: "Seis meses". Me quedé tan en shock que ni siquiera estaba triste. Hice cuentas mentalmente. Para el Mundial quedaban cuatro meses. Le dije: "¿¿¿Estás seguro???" Y él: "Mikel, lo siento. Es imposible".", cuenta el actual futbolista del Arsenal. Merino relata que "conduje hasta casa en silencio" y que "cuando le conté a mi mujer, Lola, lo que había dicho el doctor, ahí fue cuando me derrumbé. La cabeza ya lo había entendido, pero el corazón necesitaba que lo dijera en voz alta". "Los días siguientes fueron de los más duros de mi vida. Lo primero que pensé fue: No me puedo creer que me vaya a perder otro... Cuando se despejó un poco la niebla, pensé: Espera, esto tiene que haber pasado por algo", reconoce.

articles.title: Joan Gaspart recula tras su brutal rajada contra Messi, pero no pide perdón: "Me pasé"
articles.standfirst: "Le mandé un mensaje a Leo, y como lo quiero tanto.. me pasé, me pasé"
articles.summary: "Le mandé un mensaje a Leo, y como lo quiero tanto.. me pasé, me pasé"
articles.body: Joan Gaspart, presidente del F.C. Barcelona de julio de año 2000 a febrero de 2003, quiso matizar su brutal rajada contra Leo Messi en el pódcast 'Sólo Para Culés'. "Lo digo desde el amor histórico que yo tengo por un jugador que fiché cuando tenía 13 años y yo era el presidente del Barça.. Que vaya con cuidado. El Barça está por encima de su persona", fue la comentada advertencia del exdirigente culé a Messi. Gaspart declaró que "sea quien sea el presidente, que Messi venga a despedirse del Barça", y endureció su discurso al apuntar que "si Leo Messi viene a despedirse y no viene porque Laporta es el presidente y viene el día que Laporta no esté, yo no iría a ese homenaje". "¿Quién se ha creído?", subrayó. Días después Joan Gaspart ha querido aclarar, sobre sus palabras contra Messi. "¿Si voy a pedir perdón a Messi? Yo nunca les he pedido perdón a mis hijos cuando les he recriminado algo que pensaba que era lo mejor para ellos. Se puede querer a Messi tanto como yo, pero no se puede querer a Messi más que yo... Le mandé un mensaje a Leo, y como lo quiero tanto.. me pasé, me pasé. Diciéndole 'te queremos mucho, pero el Barça es más que tú'. Ahí se podía haber terminado", le contestó a Jota Jordi en ¡Sólo para Culés'.

articles.title: Lautaro Martínez desmonta las teorías conspirativas sobre la final del Mundial que ganó España
articles.standfirst: "Había gente que no podía caminar y seguía corriendo, y hasta la última jugada tuvimos posibilidad de ganarlo. Entonces, cuando se habla de esas teorías, molesta"
articles.summary: "Había gente que no podía caminar y seguía corriendo, y hasta la última jugada tuvimos posibilidad de ganarlo. Entonces, cuando se habla de esas teorías, molesta"
articles.body: Lautaro Martínez, delantero del Inter de Milán, desmonta todas las especulaciones y teorías conspirativas que se publicaron en Argentina sobre la final del Mundial 2026 que acabó ganando España por 1-0 con un histórico gol de Ferran Torres. Tras perder la final del Mundial en Argentina se llegó a poner en duda el compromiso de los jugadores de la albiceleste. "Cuando se habla de esas teorías molesta. El rival fue superior y alguna vez iba a pasar", destacó Lautaro Martínez, que no jugó ni un segundo en la final por decisión de Scaloni a pesar de ser decisivo con un gol ante Inglaterra en semifinales. Lautaro Martínez destacó que "el partido contra Inglaterra nos quitó mucha energía. Dimos hasta lo que no teníamos, y en la final también. Ver jugadores como Nico (Otamendi), como el Cuti (Romero), como Licha (Martínez), que les tocó salir, pero que han dado todo hasta lo que no tenían, como Gonzalo (Montiel), Leo (Messi), Julián (Álvarez) y así te puedo seguir nombrando porque al final, hemos dejado todo hasta lo que no teníamos y se vio reflejado". "Había gente que no podía caminar y seguía corriendo y hasta la última jugada tuvimos posibilidad de ganarlo. Entonces cuando se habla de esas teorías molesta, pero molesta en el sentido de que está reflejado que hemos dado todo y eso es lo que a nosotros nos deja tranquilos, no se dio. El rival fue superior y alguna vez iba a pasar", remarcó el tercer goleador histórico de la albiceleste. El delantero argentino apuntó en AFA Estudio que "muchos chicos llegábamos complicados. Yo tuve una lesión donde dos meses estuve afuera. En la fase eliminatoria, los alargues te consumen energía. El correr de atrás, el saber que tienes que levantar partidos, la ansiedad de la gente, el nerviosismo, todo lo que se vivía, todas las miradas estaban puestas en Argentina. Entonces, yo creo que hasta el pitazo final del último partido donde no pudimos conseguir traer la copa nuevamente a casa se vio que el equipo dejó hasta lo que no tenía".

articles.title: Morientes está "indignadísimo" con la sanción a Vinicius: "¿Qué agresión ven? Es una barbaridad"
articles.summary: Fernando Morientes, futbolista en el Real Madrid en dos etapas diferentes (1997 a 2003 y 2004 a 2005), analizó en el programa 'El Partidazo de COPE' la situación de Vinicius en el Real Madrid tras su sanción de cuatro partidos.
articles.body: Fernando Morientes, futbolista en el Real Madrid en dos etapas diferentes (1997 a 2003 y 2004 a 2005), analizó en el programa 'El Partidazo de COPE' la situación de Vinicius en el Real Madrid tras su sanción de cuatro partidos. "Estoy indignadísimo con la sanción a Vinicius. Esto esta tratado como una agresión... Me vienen a la cabeza el planchazo de Simeone a Julen Guerrero en el que le hace un agujero, la de Andoni Goikoetxea con Maradona... ¿Alguien no ve que esto no es una agresión? Es un calentón, un momento de tensión, Con dos partidos es mucho más que suficiente y cuatro son una exageración. Llevarlo al nivel de agresión... ¿Qué agresión estás viendo? Es roja directa, no hay discusión, pero cuatro partidos son una barbaridad", explica el exfutbolista, que fue formó parte del Comité de Asesores creado por la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) y el Comité Técnico de Árbitros (CTA) para seleccionar y analizar las jugadas más polémicas de cada jornada. Morientes le comentó a Juanma Castaño que cree que la sanción a Vinicius puede ser una buena oportunidad para que el brasileño recupero su mejor versión: "No hay mal que por bien no venga. A veces, estas situaciones sirven para dar oportunidades a jugadores que lo están pidiendo a gritos".

articles.title: Premier League: Is the era of the 'Big Six' coming to an end?
articles.summary: For years the Premier League has had a defined 'Big Six', comprised of Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur., but could this era be coming to an end?
articles.body:
For years the Premier League has had a defined 'Big Six', comprised of Arsenal , Chelsea , Liverpool , Manchester City , Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur .

They were not just the sides who often dominated the top positions in the table, but also had the biggest fanbase, most financial clout and were usually the league's most successful sides.

But that has not been in the case in more recent seasons.

In the last couple of years Tottenham and Manchester United have found themselves fighting at the wrong end of the table, while teams like Aston Villa , Brentford and Brighton have been battling at the top.

Meanwhile, Manchester City - the top-flight's dominant side over the past decade - are facing a period of uncertainty after the club was recently found guilty of breaching financial rules over nine years.

But is the era of the traditional 'Big Six' on the field at an end?

From Leicester fairytale to recent struggles

One of the most memorable stories of the Premier League era was Leicester City upsetting the odds to win the title in the 2015-16 season.

It captured the imagination of football fans everywhere, because it seemed so difficult for anyone outside the 'Big Six' to get even close to being champions.

But it seemed as though it was destined to be a one-off as, for the following three seasons, the 'Big Six' locked down the top positions once more.

Indeed, the gap between them and the rest was bigger than ever, with the smallest deficit between seventh and sixth place during those three seasons being eight points.

Between 2010-11 and 2018-19, the so-called 'Big Six' finished in those leading positions five times. They also finished in the top seven twice and top eight once.

In only one of the six seasons since have they all finished in the top six, with Aston Villa , Newcastle and Brighton in those places at some point.

Tottenham , in particular, have struggled and ended one place above the relegation zone in each of the past two campaigns and are currently second bottom on three points after failing to win any of their first six games.

This season, albeit early days, Manchester United are in 13th spot and Liverpool ninth. Since 2021-22, Chelsea and United have finished out of the top six twice, while Spurs have missed out three times - twice finishing 17th.

Five of the top six places have gone to clubs not in the traditional six in the past three years - the same as the previous eight years combined.

One reason for the end of their dominance as a collective is because other clubs have closed the financial gap.

Newcastle are an example following a £305m takeover led by the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund in 2021.

They went from finishing 11th in 2021-22 to fourth in the following campaign and then fifth two seasons later.

Meanwhile, others, like Brighton , have leaned into data and smart recruitment to help them close the gap.

The Seagulls have an impressive record of buying promising talent for low prices before selling them on for significant fees.

In 2021 they signed 19-year-old Ecuador midfielder Moises Caicedo from Independiente del Valle for £4m and sold him two years later to Chelsea in a deal a worth £115m - a British record at the time. They also signed Marc Cucurella for £15m and sold him to Chelsea for £62m and brought in Alexis Mac Allister for £7m before selling him to Liverpool for a deal worth £55m.

"Our recruitment strategy and philosophy has been something that we've built on over a long period of time now," sporting director Mike Cave told BBC Radio 5 Live's Football Daily podcast.

"The data element of it gets a lot of attention because going back a few years it was quite novel in comparison to some other clubs.

"Really it's just a component of a bigger process that goes on. It's an important component, it helps us to identify talent from around the world in quite an efficient way which allows us to move quickly in what is a really competitive transfer market."

How Brighton attract and develop the best young players ahead of their rivals

Has your team made the list of the world's richest football clubs?

Since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, Manchester United have struggled to get close to the success they enjoyed under the 26-year reign of the legendary Scot.

The 20-time top-flight champions have had a high turnover of head coaches in recent years in an effort to find the winning formula and since the start of the 2020-21 season they have had four different permanent managers.

But they are not alone in this high amount of chopping and changing - and not even the worst.

In the same period, Chelsea have had seven different people in charge on a permanent basis, while Tottenham have had six as they too have tried to find a way to challenge for trophies.

Meanwhile, Arsenal have shown patience can pay dividends by giving Mikel Arteta - appointed in 2019 - time to build a squad that resulted in the Gunners ending their 22-year wait for a Premier League title last season.

The 'Big Six' hasn't always been a thing in the Premier League, so an evolution of what it is and who they are was always likely to happen.

Indeed, when the league was first formed back in 1992 there was a 'Big Five' of Arsenal , Everton , Liverpool , Manchester United and Tottenham - clubs who were seen at the time as the ones with the biggest fanbase and financial power.

That evolved into a 'Big Two' during the late 1990s and early 2000s as Manchester United and Arsenal dominated, before expanding to a 'Big Four' as Chelsea and Liverpool regularly finished in the top four.

The 2010-11 season was the first time in English league history where the top six was made up of Arsenal , Chelsea , Liverpool , Manchester City , Manchester United and Tottenham .

It was then repeated in 2014-15, 2016-17, 2017-18 and 2018-19 as the 'Big Six' became known for what it is now.

Arguably the most open the top division has ever been was in the 1960s, when Burnley, Tottenham , Ipswich , Everton , Liverpool , Manchester United , Manchester City and Leeds all won league titles.

While it still feels that a Premier League winner is likely to come from one of the 'Big Six' sides, we are moving away from the concept of the top six being exclusively those sides - with it now being four years since they all finished in those positions.

Currently, Brighton , Brentford and Everton all find themselves in the top six and, while there is still a lot of football to be played this season, the top end of the division seems as open as it has ever been - and that can only be a good thing, right?

articles.title: Atlético, ritmo de campeonato
articles.standfirst: Los rojiblancos, que buscan la quinta victoria seguida, llevan a estas alturas sólo un punto menos que el año que logró su última Liga. Objetivo recortar en el Clásico
articles.summary: Los rojiblancos, que buscan la quinta victoria seguida, llevan a estas alturas sólo un punto menos que el año que logró su última Liga. Objetivo recortar en el Clásico
articles.body: Seis victorias, un empate y una derrota. Este es el balance actual del Atlético para sumar los 19 puntos que le mantienen como principal perseguidor del intratable Barça, que lleva 24 de 24, un pleno de victorias que hace imposible seguir su estela incluso firmando un arranque casi clavado al qir logró la temporada 20-21, la última que acabó con los de Simeone en lo más alto de la clasificación. Entonces, los rojiblancos apenas cedieron dos empates (Huesca y Villarreal) para sumar 20 de los 24 puntos. El empate de los de Castellón y la derrota en San Mamés dejan a este equipo marchando un ritmo muy parejo al que le valió entonces para conquistar la segunda Liga del Cholismo. Con estos números se presenta el Atlético el sábado en Cornellá, estadio donde buscará la quinta victoria seguida en el campeonato (sexta contando todas las competiciones) para seguir apretando a los de Flick, que tienen una salida complicada al campo del Betis, donde ya cayó el Real Madrid. Sumar una victoria podría acortar las diferencias justo antes de recibir al Deportivo y de rendir visita al Levante. Nueve puntos en total antes de recibir precisamente al conjunto del Camp Nou el 8 de noviembre, último partido antes del parón de selecciones. Más allá del calendario del Atlético, los de Simeone cuentan con otra bala para reducir distancias con la cabeza de la tabla. Se trata del próximo Clásico entre Barça y Madrid en el que los de Mou podrían acabar con el pleno azulgrana. Un pleno, por cierto, que los rojiblancos firmaron con Simeone en su primera Liga. Y es que en la temporada 13-14 ganaron sus ocho primeros encuentros y, cosas del calendario, perdieron su primer partido en la visita al Espanyol, el equipo al que precisamente visitan para seguir su ritmo de campeonato.

articles.title: Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler: Art dealer who went from boos to hero
articles.summary: How Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler has gone from Germany's fifth tier to being reportedly of interest to Manchester United.
articles.body:
When Brighton lost at home to Crystal Palace in February, Fabian Hurzeler was booed by his own supporters and subjected to chants of "you're getting sacked in the morning".

"There are only two options," said the German after the 1-0 defeat by their fierce rivals left his team floundering 14th in the table with one win in 12 Premier League matches.

"Give up or keep pushing harder, and that's always the option I choose in my life."

Eight months on, Brighton are reaping the benefits of keeping faith with the man who became the youngest permanent manager in Premier League history when he was appointed in June 2024 at the age of 31.

Palace return to Amex Stadium on Sunday (14:00 BST kick-off) to face opponents who are third in the table after statement wins over defending champions Arsenal and Europa League winners Aston Villa.

Hurzeler's stock has rocketed after 11 wins in 18 top-flight games, a run that has propelled the Seagulls back into Europe and left fans - who shouted "you don't know what you're doing" at him just a few months ago - worried that he could be lured away.

Following last Saturday's win at Sunderland, there was chat on the post-match phone-ins that Hurzeler, rewarded with a new long-term contract before the end of last season and given £150m to spend on signings in the summer, could be a prime target for a big club looking for a manager.

"You learn more about yourself and the people around you when you are losing games," former Brighton striker Glenn Murray told BBC Sport in reference to last season's poor run.

"Hurzeler has come out the other side and the way he has got this group of players performing is exceptional."

Scott McCarthy, from the We Are Brighton fan site, said Hurzeler appeared to have lost the crowd to such a degree at one stage last season than even a few wins would not be enough to turn it around.

"He looked like a manager who was out of ideas," McCarthy told BBC Sport.

"Leaving the stadium after losing at home to Palace, the only conversation fans were having was: 'he has got to go'.

"It's totally different now. It's worked out phenomenally."

Will Brighton manage to keep hold of Hurzeler, who has gone from managing in Germany's fifth tier to reported interest , external from Manchester United ?

Hurzeler signs to 2029 as Brighton rival elite clubs

Hurzeler's Brighton choice and Barber's favourite moment - fans' forum

The determination Hurzeler demonstrated in the face of anger from fans following last season's defeat by Palace has been evident throughout his 10-year coaching career.

In 2016, after one injury too many following spells in the reserves at Bayern Munich, Hoffenheim and 1860 Munich, the former midfielder gave up playing professionally to accept a player-manager role at German fifth-tier side Pipinsried at the age of 23.

It was the start of a coaching journey that has led to the Premier League.

To make ends meet at village club Pipinsried, which is about 30 miles from Munich, football-obsessed Hurzeler worked for an art dealer selling paintings to wealthy Bavarians.

In an interview with the Guardian , external in 2024, he revealed he was fired from that job because he was spending too much time watching games.

"If you want to sell something to a person, you have to try to convince them by doing something," he said when comparing selling pictures to managing Premier League players.

"And you can't go there and say: 'Look at this picture, it's an amazing picture'. You have to understand the needs and the wishes from the clients.

"That's a little bit similar to being a coach.

"The most important thing is to understand the person behind the player. What are his needs? What are his values? How is he educated? How was his past? Where does he get education?"

Hurzeler's obsession to succeed runs deep.

While managing St Pauli - who he left in 2024 to join Brighton after guiding the Hamburg club back to the Bundesliga following a 13-year absence , external - he was invited to Tottenham 's training ground to watch Ange Postecoglou's side train.

Hurzeler - who was born in Houston, Texas, before moving to Germany at the age of two - asked so many questions that Postecoglou had to ask another member of his coaching staff to step in and take over.

He also picked up tips from Roberto de Zerbi at Brighton , a few months before replacing him after Kieran McKenna, , external who had been heavily linked with the job, opted to stay at newly promoted Ipswich .

Despite respectable back-to-back eighth-placed finishes, Hurzeler's time at Brighton has not been without its difficult moments.

In addition to fans calling for his dismissal last season, the Seagulls were thrashed 7-0 at Nottingham Forest in his first season in charge, while former Arsenal and England defender Martin Keown labelled Hurzeler "wet behind the ears" , external on the BBC's Final Score following Brighton 's 4-2 defeat at Chelsea in September 2024.

So what is the reason for the shift in fortunes since his own fans called for his dismissal?

"It's partly because Hurzeler went back to basics," adds McCarthy.

"He relied on an experienced core in the side to get out of the hole, which is testament to him because it shows his pragmatic side. You get managers who are wedded to their philosophy and won't change.

"Hurzeler realised what he was doing was not working and that it could cost him his job, so tried something else. You can now see this is a team more in his image, because they press insanely."

Will Hurzeler leave Brighton if another club comes for him, or stay and attempt to write his name in club folklore by qualifying for the Champions League?

"I personally don't think he will go," says McCarthy.

"The money would obviously be tempting but he is a very intelligent guy. He didn't become a Premier League manager at the age of 31 without having his head screwed on.

"Does he want to go to another club where he isn't going to get time? What has happened at Brighton has shown he needs two-and-a-half-years to build a squad."

Back in Pipinsried, Hurzeler's name is still revered - and he has not forgotten where his coaching journey began.

"Yes, he does enjoy coming back every now and then - to see if everything's in order," Sepp Ankner, their chief finance officer, told The Athletic , external in 2024.

"When he does, he talks to everybody. He's really retained that connection with Pipinsried."

But his rapid ascent means gilded surroundings might not be far away for Europe's hottest managerial property.

articles.title: Ser delantero del Valencia, hoy: solo un gol de un '9'... mientras sí rinden en los otros 19 equipos
articles.standfirst: Mal momento para los arietes del Valencia que no logran cumplir con su mayor reto que es marcar lo que les lleva a la cola de todos los equipos de la Liga
articles.summary: Mal momento para los arietes del Valencia que no logran cumplir con su mayor reto que es marcar lo que les lleva a la cola de todos los equipos de la Liga
articles.body: El inicio de temporada del Valencia está siendo empinada. La revolución total tras la quinta jornada que llevó a las destituciones masivas en el área deportiva. Pero los problemas siguen. Y la delantera lo es. No hay forma de que cumplan con su rol tras ocho jornadas. Los atacantes han podido marcar sólo un gol. El de Sadiq ante el Dépor en Riazor. No hay un solo equipo de Primera división cuyos delanteros hayan marcado uno o ningún gol en el cómputo global. Esto refleja la forma de trabajar la plantilla a lo largo del verano en la que se ha errado en muchas decisiones tomadas de ahí una plantilla descompensada. El delantero nigeriano fue el autor del único tanto de un 'nueve'. Porque ni Hugo Duro ni Danjuma, que llegó a Mestalla con la vitola de artillero, lo han hecho. De momento, no han conseguido perforar la meta rival. Y eso que han tenido ocasiones para hacerlo pero han estado aciagos. El contraste viene con los restantes 19 conjuntos de Primera división en los que sus delanteros han ido dando la talla. Esta es la lista de equipos que han marcado hasta el momento en esta temporada Curiosamente Sadiq, que ha sido el único delantero que ha marcado en este ejercicio, cayó lesionado precisamente en Riazor el pasado 30 de agosto. E iba para dos meses. “Ahora creo que estoy a punto de volver. Ya solo me quedan algunos pasos y estaré con el equipo”, señaló hace pocos días en un acto. Y Aguirre lo espera 'como agua de mayo'.

articles.title: 1.FC Union Berlin vs. Borussia Dortmund preview: Kovač sets out to make amends
articles.summary: 1.FC Union BerlinSaturday's battle at the Stadion an der Alten Försterei throws up an interesting encounter between hosts 1.FC Union Berlin and visitors Boru...
articles.body:
Saturday's battle at the Stadion an der Alten Försterei throws up an interesting encounter between hosts 1.FC Union Berlin and visitors Borussia Dortmund. Kick-off gets underway at 15:30 CET on Bundesliga Matchday 6.

Adding an extra layer of spice to this fixture, Mauro Lustrinelli picked up his first win as coach of the Köpenick outfit last weekend. A marked improvement on previous efforts, with Livan Burcu's goal downing Elversberg 1-0.

The result seemed to have galvanized the club from the German capital. Now, continuity is the next step, with Lustrinelli unlikely to alter that same winning formula too much unless Emmanuel Latte Lath is fit to replace Skarke.

Although their form hasn't been perfect thus far, Union Berlin can take some confidence into this specific meeting. Die Eisernen have won four of their seven Bundesliga clashes with the Westphalian giants whilst on home soil.

Stanley Nsoki (muscle injury), Andrik Markgraf (ACL) and Josip Juranovic (illness) look likely to sit this one out. Andrej Ilic (food poisoning) and Emmanuel Latte Lath (muscular issues) face a race against time to be available.

Moving onto the visitors, Borussia Dortmund started the campaign on fire but that spark has failed to flicker in recent weeks. In fact, their turn in form seems to have coincided with the lengthy October international break.

Their run of four consecutive wins in the top flight came to an end when Ludovic Reis and Niclas Füllkrug struck for Werder Bremen in a 2-2 draw. Things didn't improve during midweek either as BVB met another setback.

Niko Kovač's ambitious rotation for a tricky trip to Bodø/Glimt in the Arctic Circle went up in smoke. The five changes, largely in attack, went against the Westphalians who suffered a 1-0 loss thanks to Fredrik Sjøvold's strike.

Kovač now finds himself under pressure, hunting a win in Berlin. A victory would likely lift the gloom off his squad ahead of a busy schedule. Still, most recent trips to Köpenick have been far from a one-sided affairs.

Emre Can and Giannis Konstantelias (both ACL tears) remain the two long-term absentees for BVB. Justin Lerma (muscular problems) is also out, however Nico Schlotterbeck should be back after a rest during midweek.

articles.title: Wild development in Liverpool's big Endrick pursuit
articles.summary: Liverpool did try to sign Endrick back in the summer. That didn't work out - and now things have seen a wild development.Liverpool made an attempt to sign En...
articles.body:
Liverpool did try to sign Endrick back in the summer. That didn't work out - and now things have seen a wild development.

Liverpool made an attempt to sign Endrick back in the summer. Fabrizio Romano confirmed that recently as the Reds were one of a few clubs who felt his time at Real Madrid was up.

And they had good reason to believe that. Endrick has barely gotten opportunities at the club and spent the second half of last season out on loan with Lyon.

We think his time out there went seriously under the radar and was much, much better than people think . Enough that we'd have prioritised his arrival back in the summer.

The fact that Real Madrid also signed Carlos Espi from Levante suggested that Endrick just wouldn't get a look-in but the Brazilian opted to stick it out. He's still there and, up until recently, failing to get involved.

Real Madrid played out a ridiculous UEFA Champions League meeting with AS Roma on Wednesday evening. Los Blancos were 3-1 down with 10 minutes to play but somehow turned it around to win 4-3.

And Endrick played an enormous role in that. He got 31 minutes in Rome which is, quite astonishingly, 27 more minutes than he's had in every other game this season combined.

He made the most of it. Endrick scored one with a header from a corner and got the sort-of-assist for Espi's goal, also off a corner - as in, it was his effort at goal that the goalkeeper spilled for Espi to slot home.

So here we had decisive moments from Endrick, in a truly wild game, with what was his only serious football of the season so far. And that's quite a twist as we imagine it will suddenly propel him back into contention.

It all looked over and done with for Endrick, as reports in Spain all suggested that he was destined to leave and unable to get any minutes. His lack of minutes, which again stood at four total minutes across all competitions , helped the player finally realise that he wasn't going to get chances.

And then, out of nowhere, as a last throw of the dice, he proves his worth. We'll see how things develop from here but what looked like a golden opportunity for Liverpool to sign Endrick suddenly looks a lot more muddled.

articles.title: Jude Bellingham reaches double milestone in Real Madrid’s 4-3 comeback win vs Roma
articles.summary: Real Madrid midfield star Jude Bellingham reached a significant milestone during Los Blancos’ thrilling 4-3 comeback victory over AS Roma, making his 150th a...
articles.body:
Real Madrid midfield star Jude Bellingham reached a significant milestone during Los Blancos' thrilling 4-3 comeback victory over AS Roma , making his 150th appearance for the club.

Furthermore, the result also marked his 100th win in a Real Madrid shirt, giving the Englishman two achievements to celebrate in the same match.

In the same game, Vinicius Jr. also reached a major landmark against the Italian side, recording his 250th victory for Real Madrid.

Bellingham records 150 Real Madrid appearances and 100 wins

Bellingham reached the 150-game mark during his fourth season at Real Madrid, having scored 49 goals for the club.

His 150 appearances are spread across six competitions: 95 in La Liga, 35 in the Champions League, six in the Copa del Rey, seven in the Club World Cup, six in the Spanish Super Cup and one in the UEFA Super Cup.

Bellingham's 100 victories are similarly distributed across domestic and international competitions.

Vinicius celebrates 250 Real Madrid wins

As noted before, Vinicius reached his own landmark during the 4-3 victory, recording his 250th win for Real Madrid. The Brazilian forward has played 385 matches for the club and scored 129 goals.

His first victory came on October 31, 2018, when Real Madrid defeated UD Melilla 4-0 in the Copa del Rey. Since then, Vinicius has become a central figure in the club's success, winning 14 titles.

Vinicius records his 250th Real Madrid win against Roma. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images)

His trophy collection includes two Champions League titles, three Club World Cups, two UEFA Super Cups, three La Liga titles, one Copa del Rey and three Spanish Super Cups.

How Vinicius' 250 victories are distributed

La Liga accounts for the largest share of Vinicius' victories, with 167 wins in the competition.

He has also registered 51 victories in the Champions League, 16 in the Copa del Rey, eight in the Club World Cup, six in the Spanish Super Cup and two in the UEFA Super Cup.

The milestones for Bellingham and Vinicius came during a memorable night against Roma, with both players continuing to build impressive records at Real Madrid.

articles.title: Pointless Celtic, Dermot Desmond’s participators crumble in Lisbon
articles.summary: Benfica 4-1 Celtic – Another European failure, when will it ever end?Camilo Duran of Celtic FC looks on during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD...
articles.body:
Benfica 4-1 Celtic – Another European failure, when will it ever end?

Camilo Duran of Celtic FC looks on during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between SL Benfica vs Celtic FC at Estádio do Lisboa e Benfica on October 15th,2026 Photo by Joao Bravo/Sports IMAGO

Another European night, and yet another abject failure as we crashed 4-1 to Benfica in Lisbon, leaving us pointless after the first two games in the Europa League.

Once again we made life difficult for ourselves, going behind after just five minutes after Dane Murray conceded a spot kick, and from then on in we knew it was going to be a very long night.

The fact that each and everyone of us knew it was curtains at such an early stage tells you everything you need to know about this Celtic side, who looked devoid of not only quality, but any sort of self belief.

We look very much like a side that doesn't really know what the hell they should be doing. Maybe just maybe, Cameron Carter Vickers was speaking the truth with his post match remarks after the home loss to the Rangers?

It certainly looked like it from the first whistle in Lisbon last night, as a quality filled Benfica side took advantage of our inability to even do the basics.

Celtic were 3-0 down at the break, and staring down the barrel of yet another heavy European defeat, with our main objective in the second half simply to keep the scoreline respectable.

We did improve a little after the interval, but it was all a little too late as the damage had already been inflicted in the first forty five minutes.

Listen, no one expected us to get a result last night, but the manner in which we lost that we can't abide. Last night they embarrassed the Hoops – in Lisbon of all places – but we are know that the club is there to participate rather than compete.

What we want to see is a side who are up for the fight, one that makes their opponents work hard for their win, and yet again we didn't see any of those qualities last night, and not for the first time in a big European night we had to witness a total embarrassment on the park from a Celtic side.

We can only ask, when will it ever end? The answer to that goes beyond a rookie centre-half, or a record signing who can't contribute or a manager whose time as an elite coach has faded as the game moved forward. It certainly doesn't land with the Celtic support who were magnificent in Lisbon. No it lies in the controlling shareholder who is strangling the life out of Celtic's ambition.

articles.title: Romano: One top Man Utd official pushing to appoint ‘meticulous’ EPL head coach
articles.summary: With Manchester United pondering another mid-season managerial appointment, Fabrizio Romano confirms Fabian Hurzeler is one of the names thrown in the hat.Mi...
articles.body:
With Manchester United pondering another mid-season managerial appointment, Fabrizio Romano confirms Fabian Hurzeler is one of the names thrown in the hat.

Michael Carrick enjoyed a stellar start to his reign after taking over from Ruben Amorim in January. The 45-year-old led the team to a comfortable third-place finish, thus securing Champions League qualification.

The former Man Utd midfielder thus earned himself a permanent contract. However, the club's woeful start to the new campaign is putting his job under increasing scrutiny .

Fabian Hurzeler wanted by Man Utd official

Man Utd currently find themselves 13th in the league table, having only registered one win in six Premier League outings. They also suffered an embarrassing elimination from the Carabao Cup at the hands of Brighton despite taking an early two-goal lead.

Speaking of the Seagulls, they have been the main Dark Horses of the new campaign, registering sensational results between domestic competitions and the Conference League.

Therefore, Hurzeler has been highly praised for his 'meticulous' work at the club, undoubtedly attracting the interest of several top clubs.

In the latest video uploaded on his YouTube channel, Italian journalist Fabrizio Romano confirmed that one Man Utd official has been advocating for the 33-year-old.

"There is one specific person in the Manchester United leadership group, who really appreciates Fabian Hürzeler," said the transfer market guru.

"He is bringing his name into the conversation when they talk about the managerial situation and talented managers."

Nevertheless, Romano clarifies that the decision to sack Carrick has yet to be taken, so these internal talks are only precautionary so that the club isn't caught unprepared in case they decide to take drastic measures in the coming weeks.

Moreover, the journalist insists that United have yet to make any contact with Hurzeler or his entourage, while also naming three other candidates in Antonio Conte, who has already expressed his openness to return to management in mid-season, plus the currently unattached Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe.

Two years ago, Man Utd sacked Erik ten Hag and convinced a young manager to abandon his successful project mid-season to oversee the chaos at Carrington.

In hindsight, this proved to be a misstep in Ruben Amorim's managerial career, although he managed to land the AC Milan job in the summer.

Hurzeler represents an even younger profile (33), albeit with Premier League experience, having coached Brighton for almost 100 games since joining the club in 2024.

At this stage, it feels that United are crying out for a highly experienced manager with a proven track record and the ability to squeeze the best out of underperforming players. Hence why Conte would arguably be the most suited for the role, at least amid the current circumstances.

articles.body:
It was a special evening for José Mourinho at the Olimpico. Not only were his former fans paying tribute, but he also met with the survivors of his Giallorossi squad: Dybala, Mancini, and Pellegrini.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport reports on newsstands today, the Special One greeted his three former players in the Olimpico parking lot, sharing jokes, hugs, and smiles with them as the Blancos fought back against Roma.

The most important meeting, however, was with Lorenzo Pellegrini. Their embrace was indeed charged with meaning after the rumors circulating after the Portuguese's dismissal that the midfielder and the Portuguese coach had deteriorated.

Undoubtedly a special match for Mourinho, who was able to relive, even if only for one evening, the emotions that only the Olimpico can offer.

Juventus have won six of their last eight matches in UEFA major competitions (1D, 1L), as many wins as they have in their previous 21 (8D, 7L).

Randal Kolo Muani has scored back-to-back appearances across all competitions for the first time since May-June 2025: scoring against Venezia in Serie A and Al Ain at the Club World Cup, also with Juventus.

Pierre Kalulu has crossed the milestone of 100 appearances in all competitions with the Juventus shirt (72 Serie A, 18 Champions League, 4 Club World Cup, 3 Coppa Italia, 2 Europa League and 1 Super Cup).

Nick Woltemade became only the second Juventus player to score in both of his first two appearances in a major UEFA competition in the 21st century (since 2001), after Daniel Osvaldo (in February 2014 in the Europa League).

articles.title: Van Gaal acusa al Manchester City y sus 114 trampas de su "sufrimiento"
articles.standfirst: "No puedo volver atrás en el tiempo; ni siquiera la Federación Inglesa de Fútbol puede hacerlo"
articles.summary: "No puedo volver atrás en el tiempo; ni siquiera la Federación Inglesa de Fútbol puede hacerlo"
articles.body: Louis van Gaal, exentrenador del F.C. Barcelona, ha atribuido el "sufrimiento" que padeció durante su tormentosa salida del Manchester United en 2016 al "dopaje financiero" por 114 infracciones del Manchester City. El técnico neerlandés fue despedido por los Glazer al final de la temporada 2015-16, en la que los 'Red Devils' ganaron la FA Cup pero se quedaron a las puertas de clasificarse para la Champions League. City y United terminaron la Premier League con 66 puntos, pero los 'citizens' que entonces entrenaba Manuel Pellegrini se metió en Champions por su mejor diferencia de goles. "Para mí, en aquel momento, eso (no lograr la clasificación para la Liga de Campeones en 2016) fue probablemente el factor determinante en mi destitución del Manchester United, con todas las consecuencias y el sufrimiento que ello conllevó", comunicó Van Gaal (75 años) en un correo electrónico que envió a 'The Athletic'. Louis van Gaal, que tras su marcha del United pasó un año sabático y no volvió a entrenar hasta 2021, destacó que "sin duda" las cosas podrían haber sido distintas si hubiera competido en un entorno justo. La etapa del técnico neerlandés en Old Trafford coincidió con el periodo comprendido entre 2009 y 2018, durante el cual se determinó que el Manchester City había inflado artificialmente sus ingresos mediante patrocinios. "No puedo volver atrás en el tiempo; ni siquiera la Federación Inglesa de Fútbol puede hacerlo", reconoció. Respecto a la posible sanción que debería recibir el Manchester City apuntó que "es el juez quien debe decidir".

articles.title: Betis y Porto unen experiencias para impulsar el impacto social del fútbol
articles.standfirst: La Fundación y el club portugués han compartido conocimientos y buenas prácticas en una jornada centrada en la inclusión, la sostenibilidad y el compromiso social
articles.summary: La Fundación y el club portugués han compartido conocimientos y buenas prácticas en una jornada centrada en la inclusión, la sostenibilidad y el compromiso social
articles.body: La Fundación Real Betis Balompié, el FC Porto y su Fundación han compartido experiencias durante la visita del club portugués a Sevilla, con el objetivo de intercambiar conocimientos sobre sus proyectos sociales, deportivos y medioambientales. Durante el encuentro, la delegación del Porto conoció iniciativas verdiblancas centradas en la inclusión, la sostenibilidad y la accesibilidad, como el equipo de fútbol para personas amputadas y el Real Betis Genuine, que promueven la integración y el desarrollo personal a través del deporte. El encuentro incluyó una visita a la Ciudad Deportiva Rafael Gordillo y al ecohuerto vinculado a Forever Green, la plataforma de sostenibilidad ambiental del Betis. Este recorrido ha permitido compartir experiencias sobre la integración de prácticas sostenibles en el ámbito deportivo y conocer cómo el fútbol puede contribuir a la concienciación y protección del medioambiente. Una colaboración enriquecedora para ambas instituciones, que comparten la convicción de que los clubes de fútbol pueden desempeñar un papel fundamental en la construcción de una sociedad más inclusiva y sostenible. Uno de los momentos más especiales de la jornada ha sido el protagonizado por Martim, un aficionado del Porto con autismo al que la Fundación Real Betis Balompié ha invitado a acompañar a su equipo durante su viaje a Sevilla. Gracias a la Sala Sensorial del Real Betis, Martim ha podido viajar por primera vez con el club portugués y disfrutar de esta experiencia junto a su equipo. Es un ejemplo de cómo la colaboración entre clubes puede ir más allá de los terrenos de juego y traducirse en experiencias que favorecen la inclusión y la participación. Ambas entidades están vinculadas a iniciativas europeas como Free Kicks, centrada en promover la economía circular y las prácticas sostenibles en el fútbol, y GARFIELD, orientada a combatir el greenwashing y fomentar una comunicación medioambiental más rigurosa y transparente en el deporte. Estos proyectos reflejan la importancia de establecer alianzas entre organizaciones deportivas europeas para compartir conocimientos, impulsar buenas prácticas y afrontar de manera conjunta los retos sociales y medioambientales del sector. Con este encuentro, la Fundación Real Betis Balompié reafirma su voluntad de seguir construyendo redes de colaboración con otras entidades deportivas y de aprender de experiencias que contribuyan a mejorar sus propios proyectos. Una apuesta por un fútbol que, además de competir, sea capaz de compartir, generar oportunidades y transformar realidades.

articles.title: Jason Wilcox finds himself under exact same pressure as last time Manchester United visited Elland Road to face Leeds
articles.summary: Jason Wilcox back under pressure following Lisandro Martinez's recent comments; Wilcox was in spotlight the last time Man Utd travelled to Elland Road in Ruben Amorim's final game; Watch Leeds vs Man Utd live on Sky Sports on Super Sunday from 1pm; kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
Michael Carrick's under pressure. The players are under pressure. And perhaps there is no one more under pressure than Jason Wilcox.

The club's director of football was the target of Lisandro Martinez's post-match outburst following the defeat to Atletico Madrid in midweek, with the Argentine singling him out for not doing enough to prepare for the club's return to the Champions League.

Martinez issued an apology on Thursday after internal talks, and Wilcox still has the backing of his bosses at Old Trafford. But he must be starting to think there is something in the Yorkshire water as he was also the centre of controversy the last time Manchester United visited Leeds.

Rewind back to the start of the year. The two sides played out a rather unremarkable 1-1 draw. Matheus Cunha cancelling out Brenden Aaronson's opener. However, the big talking point came during the post-match press conference.

Ruben Amorim was the man in the away dugout that day, and defended his position in sensational fashion.

"I came here to be the manager of Manchester United. Not to be the coach. That is clear," Amorim reiterated to journalists.

"I know that my name is not [Thomas] Tuchel, it's not [Antonio] Conte, it's not [Jose] Mourinho, but I'm the manager of Manchester United and it's going to be like this for 18 months or when the board decides to change."

Two days later, Amorim was sacked. Then came the details of the explosive meeting with Wilcox that appeared to be the beginning of the end.

Ahead of the trip to Elland Road, a meeting was held between the two where Amorim's tactical approach was discussed in detail.

Sky Sports News understands Amorim's 'emotional and inconsistent behaviour' was a key factor in the decision and a refusal to adapt and evolve his preferred 3-4-3 system led to a breakdown in confidence.

Ultimately, the decision to fire Amorim was one that put an end to in-house tension, but not one that would cause fireworks among the fanbase. Results under the Portuguese had not been convincing across his 14-month tenure.

That would be further justified when Carrick came in and secured Champions League football during his interim spell. He was subsequently handed the permanent gig by Wilcox and co.

Having seen the positive work that Carrick had already overseen, the change in fortune since means fans, like Martinez, are starting to look above the head coach for an answer.

An outlay of £163m was the investment into the squad thanks to the signings of Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba.

Was that enough to 'back' Carrick? Martinez didn't think so, but Wilcox certainly does.

Speaking in a message published to the club's website following Tielemans' arrival, he said: "Last season, I wrote about the sense of responsibility to help get this great club back to the top.

"A year on, we can be proud of the progress we have made towards our ultimate goals. We have taken great strides forward and can be confident that we have the right structures and processes in place to achieve regular and sustained success in the future.

"We can all be proud of the winning culture that is developing at Carrington as we continue to build a talented and determined group of players ready to compete across all four competitions."

Since those words, United have had a record-breaking start to the Premier League campaign for all the wrong reasons. They were eliminated from the Carabao Cup at the point of entry. Ironically, Wilcox watched the exact same events unfold last season.

Elland Road was where things all came to a head under Amorim. After Martinez's comments, the same could be said again. This time though, the problem can't just be removed, even with the apology.

Does this force Wilcox's hand to open up further dialogue with supporters? As Sky Sports News' Danyal Khan pointed out, it would be appreciated.

"The shame is that there has been a lack of clear communication from the leadership. I know they do the in-house media sometimes. Jason Wilcox will do an interview here and there, but I really think it's missed," Khan said in a special Sky Sports vodcast .

"Any time I go to Old Trafford, that's the issue. They want more clear communication. I don't know the reason why they haven't done that. But, I think if Wilcox did a day of media in pre-season, that would've gone a long way with fans."

Away to Leeds is always a tough game for United. The last two occasions, Wilcox has been the man in the spotlight.

In January, he found his way out by sacking Amorim. Squashing the beef with Martinez is his attempt to do the same now. Question is, will it be enough if United's dismal form continues?

The longer things don't change on the pitch, the more Martinez's original outburst will appear to ring true with supporters. Now that he has specifically been brought up by a player, it will be a lot harder for him to shift the blame.
